ai.description: This small frog reaches 3–4 cm. It is brown with a dark lateral stripe and a pointed snout. Distinctive features include long, slender limbs for leaping and prominent dorsolateral folds.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indirana leithii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark lateral band extending from the snout through the eye to the shoulder, lacking a white lip line.
ai.habitat: *Indirana leithii* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Northern Western Ghats, typically found near rocky stream beds at altitudes of 600–1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Matherana Leaping Frog is primarily nocturnal, exhibiting remarkable agility as it leaps across mossy rocks and vegetation near mountain streams to hunt small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana leithii* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 150–300 eggs on moist rocks near streams. The larvae develop terrestrially in damp, splash-zone habitats.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Matherana Leaping Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting high-elevation forests in Maharashtra and Karnataka.
ai.callDescription: The Matherana Leaping Frog emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "tink" notes, typically heard near rocky streams and waterfalls in the Western Ghats.
